newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - TI aims for top 3 polymer status.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - TI aims for top 3 polymer status.

text.p: British engineering firm TI Group Plc said on Monday that its 189 million stg acquisiton of Sweden's Forsheda was aimed at making the group one of the world's top three suppliers of polymer-engineered industrial seals in its chosen areas.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, Tony Sumner, director of corporate affairs, said: "We are looking to develop our world leadership position. We have already got a substantial position and Forsheda fits exactly with that."
Sumner said TI's aim is "to be in the top three in the niche markets we serve".

Forsheda provides seals for a variety of uses, with around 70 percent of its output directed to general industrial uses, 25 percent going to the automotive industry and five percent to the defence industry.

It will complement TI's John Crane division, which specialises in mechanical and marine seals as well as polymer engineering. TI said the agreed merger of the two sides would create a business with annual sales of around 300 million stg.
Sumner said Forsheda will benefit from TI's international focus, while TI will be able to use Forsheda's strength in Scandinavia and other parts of Europe to increase penetration of its own products.
Around 80 percent of Forsheda's sales are currently made in Europe.

He said the business would continue to expand through a mix of organic growth and bolt-on acquisitions. "They will grow organically, but we will continue to look for opportunities that will expand our process or product skills and our marketing depth."

Sumner added that "there is lots of scope" for further bolt-on acquisitions for all its key business areas, which include Bundy International, maker of fluid systems for vehicles and refrigerators, and Dowty Aerospace.
The company said the Forsheda purchase brings total bolt-on acquisitions so far this year to 240 million stg, including the expansion of its Bundy division in Brazil and South Africa.
